GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2019-08-30T15:20:07Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Attachment file size showing higher than the actual size
Description: Hi,
I am trying to check the attachments size before downloading the complete message. For this I have used the MessageSummaryItems.BodyStructure while Fetching the items from inbox. As follows.

```csharp
var items = folder.Fetch (ids, MessageSummaryItems.BodyStructure | MessageSummaryItems.UniqueId);
foreach (var item in items) {
    foreach (var attachment in item.Attachments) {
        // 'octets' is just a fancy word for "number of bytes"
        var size = attachment.Octets;
	log.Info(size);
    }
}
```

But, looking at the log, it shows the file size as more than the actual file size. Log comes as follows.

Found 2 attachments with the mail (UniqueID:5533)
Individual attachment size for message:5533 is :: 3427408
Individual attachment size for message:5533 is :: 2875804
Total size of attachment for message:5533 is 6303212

But the actual file size in File Properties shows as 2504642 and 2101546 respectively.

Can you please help me understand why the size shows more than the actual size when we download it from the email? If this is an expected behavior, is there a way to get the actual file size before downloading the attachments?

My requirement is to put a limit on the email attachment size, and ignore those emails if the size is above the limit.

The user is trying to implement attachment size limits and is confused about why the API reports larger sizes than what the files actually are when downloaded.

This is primarily a conceptual issue about how MIME attachments work in email. The solution would involve explaining that email attachments in MIME format include additional overhead (headers, encoding overhead from base64/quoted-printable encoding, etc.) that makes the raw size reported by the API larger than the resulting file after decoding.

To verify a solution to this issue, one doesn't need to build or run code - an expert can simply explain the technical reason for the discrepancy and provide guidance on how to account for this when implementing size limits.
